title: LangGraph Platform Pricing: Plans and Costs in 2026
summary: LangGraph platform pricing starts with free options and scales to enterprise plans. Determine which tier matches your usage and budget requirements.
body_markdown:
## Fix agent cost sprawl with Activepieces


### When a workflow replaces the hosted graph


If your agent mostly reads and writes business apps and calls a language model at only a few steps, an Activepieces workflow can replace the hosted graph, and the per-node arithmetic mostly stops mattering: Plus is $20 a month flat for 10,000 credits, and a run is one credit however many steps it has.


Activepieces has a core under the MIT licence, set out in the LICENSE file of its GitHub repository, with only the` packages/ee/` directories under a separate commercial licence, and it is self-hostable, so you can run it on infrastructure you already pay for and see the bill before you commit.


### What the workflow looks like


The screenshot shows the shape of that fit. A five-step workflow runs from a webhook trigger, to a database read, to an "Ask ChatGPT" step, to an SMS send, to a database write.


The selected step holds a question field with support-agent instructions and a business-details block describing StoreX, an Apple repair shop open 8am to 10pm Pacific. Only one of the five steps calls a model, so model latency becomes your limiting factor.


The other four are plumbing, and plumbing's the part you least want metered like reasoning.


### What it costs to run


Pricing it is easy: one model call per run, plus whatever your host charges for the machine. There's no graph to keep alive between requests and no tracing layer to pay extra for.


The business context lives in a text field you can read and edit, so a support-bot change is a text edit rather than a redeploy.


### Where it stops fitting


The fit has limits. Long-running agents that checkpoint state, pause for a human, and resume mid-graph are what LangGraph is built for, and Activepieces's 746 integrations don't change that; a workflow builder won't reproduce it.


The two also combine well. Keep LangGraph for the reasoning loop, and let Activepieces handle the tool layer: the database reads, the SMS sends, the app writes, split across as many small flows as you like, since every plan, including free, allows unlimited flows.


That keeps the metered graph small, and the small graph is the cheaper one.
